title: Changelog build
description: One build per file, at changelog/<stream>/<version>.json.

$schema.description: Editor hint only, pointing at this file. The server ignores it; any other key it does not know is refused.

version.description: Required. `YYYY.MDD.N`, where MDD is the release day with the month not padded (101 = January 1st) or both padded (1009 = October 9th), optionally followed by `-suffix`, the stream the build was made for, such as `2026.1009.0-g0v0`; a suffix has to match the directory the file sits in, which tools/validate.py checks because a schema cannot see the directory. The release date is read from here when `created_at` is absent.

id.description: Build identifier, and what `GET /changelog/{version}?key=id` addresses. Derived from the digits of `version` when absent; declare it to keep two builds apart when they spell the same digits.

display_version.description: Version the client shows. Defaults to `version` with the `-suffix` and every non-numeric character removed.

created_at.description: Release time. Defaults to the date carried by `version`, at midnight UTC.

users.description: Number of users running this build, as counted at release. These counts are the only source of a stream's `user_count`, which the server sums over the stream's builds; they belong here, next to the build they describe. Defaults to 0.

youtube_id.description: Video shown above the changelog, as the bare YouTube identifier rather than a URL.

entries.description: Changes shipped by this build, in the order they should be listed. At least one: a build that lists nothing is a file left half-written.

link.description: Served as written. An absolute URL is the useful value; nothing resolves a relative one.

github_user.description: Who authored the change. Every field is optional, but an empty object carries nothing and is refused.

entry.description: One change. `type` says how the client marks it; `title` or `message` says what it was, and an entry with neither is refused.

id.description: Derived from the build and the position when absent.

type.description: Required. `add` for something new, `fix` for something repaired, `misc` for anything else. The client has an icon per type and nothing for the rest, so an unknown one is refused rather than filed under `misc`.

category.description: Group heading the entry is listed under.

title.description: One line. Required unless `message` is set.

message.description: Markdown body, shown under the title. Returned as null unless the request asks for the markdown format.

url.description: Where the change can be read, when it is not a pull request.

repository.description: `owner/name` of the repository the change landed in.

github_url.description: Pull request the change came from.

major.description: Marks the change as notable in the client.
